title: The interpreter as developer: An autoethnographic design study of building a computer-assisted interpreting tool through human-LLM co-creation
abstract: arXiv:2610.16460v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Computer-assisted interpreting (CAI) tools are built for interpreters, mainly by third parties, and the interpreters' own side of development has received little first-person documentation. This article reports an autoethnographic design study in which a professional conference interpreter without formal programming training built a local-first CAI system through expert-led human-LLM co-creation. Analysis of the development dialogues shows how tacit professional knowledge became design only after generic defaults had failed in use, a reversal of the usual direction of technological mediation, from adopting tools to authoring them. Three mechanisms of in-booth appropriation emerged under a human-led division of labor, and a four-layer reconstruction illustrates the human contribution at work. First-month telemetry, over six thousand utterances across nine sessions, shows a fully local system sustaining translation-stage latencies near

translated_title: 译员作为开发者：通过人-大语言模型共创构建计算机辅助口译工具的自我民族志设计研究
translated_abstract: 计算机辅助口译（CAI）工具是为译员而构建的，主要由第三方开发，而译员自身参与开发的一面鲜有第一人称的一手记录。本文报告了一项自我民族志设计研究：一位没有接受过正规编程训练的职业会议口译员，通过以专家为主导的人-大语言模型（LLM）共创方式，构建了一个本地优先的CAI系统。对开发对话的分析表明，默会的专业知识只有在通用默认设置在实际使用中失灵之后才转化为设计——这颠覆了通常的技术中介方向，即从“采用工具”转变为“编写工具”。在人主导的分工之下，涌现出三种“口译箱内挪用”机制，四层重构则阐明了人的贡献如何在实际工作中体现。首月遥测数据——九个场次共六千余条话语——显示该完全本地化的系统将翻译阶段的延迟维持在接近（原文此处截断）……
tldr: 这项自我民族志研究表明，没有编程背景的职业口译员能够通过人-大语言模型共创实现从工具采用者到工具作者的转变，将默会的口译专业知识转化为完全本地化计算机辅助口译系统的设计。
en_tdlr: An autoethnographic study shows that a professional interpreter without formal programming training can shift from tool adopter to tool author through human-LLM co-creation, turning tacit interpreting expertise into the design of a fully local computer-assisted interpreting system.
